::: {.lead-text}
I am an applied mathematician at INSA Toulouse, where I develop fast and
reliable reduced-order models for flows governed by partial differential
equations, with a particular focus on flood simulation.
:::

## My path

I studied mathematical engineering at Sultan Moulay Slimane University in
Morocco, then moved to France for a master's degree in applied mathematics at
the Université de Pau et des Pays de l'Adour, specializing in modeling and
numerical simulation. My master's internship at INSA Toulouse, on
physics-informed machine learning for reduced-order models, set the
direction of my research.

I then did my PhD at INSA Toulouse, within the Institut de Mathématiques de
Toulouse, on reduced-order models for the two-dimensional shallow-water
equations, applied to real flood events. Since 2024, I have been a Teaching
and Research Associate (ATER) at INSA Toulouse, where I continue this
research and teach mathematics and numerical methods to engineering students.

## PhD

::: {.project-card}
[Defended · March 24, 2026]{.status .status-published}

### Reduction of the two-dimensional shallow-water equations using an error-aware POD–neural-network method: application to flood dynamics

PhD in Applied Mathematics, University of Toulouse – INSA Toulouse,
Institut de Mathématiques de Toulouse (IMT).

Supervised by Jérôme Monnier (director), Robin Bouclier (co-director) and
Pierre-André Garambois (co-supervisor, INRAE). Part of the ANR MUFFINS
project.

## Short bio

For conference programs and seminar announcements, feel free to use:

::: {.short-bio}
Mustapha Allabou is a Teaching and Research Associate in applied mathematics
at INSA Toulouse and the Institut de Mathématiques de Toulouse. He received
his PhD from INSA Toulouse in 2026. His research focuses on reduced-order
modeling and scientific machine learning for PDE-governed systems, with
applications to shallow-water flows and flood forecasting.
:::
